Keeping peptides cool in Riverside County

Riverside Municipal Airport, about 2.8 miles west-northwest of the city's center point, is the reference station for the city.36 Its 1991 to 2020 normals give August an average high of 94.9 °F and low of 64.7 °F, and December a high of 66.8 °F and low of 42.8 °F.3 The airport averages 100.5 days a year at 90 °F or more and 21.7 days at 100 °F or more, but only 3.5 nights at or below freezing.2 Riverside Fire Station 3, about 0.9 miles from the city's center point, runs hotter: 28.0 days a year at 100 °F or more.76

The county is far less even than the city. The table pairs our western pages with NOAA normals stations within about 10 miles of them; distances come from NOAA station and Census coordinates.86

NOAA station (1991 to 2020 normals) Close to Days at 90 °F or more Days at 100 °F or more
Fallbrook 5 NE Temecula, Murrieta 60.39 8.99
Chino Airport Corona 99.010 23.310
Riverside Municipal Airport Riverside 100.52 21.72
Redlands Moreno Valley 104.111 26.011
Elsinore Lakeland Village, Menifee, Temescal Valley 123.012 42.312
Palm Springs the low desert 183.04 122.74

Fallbrook's normals rest on about 12 years of data within the 30-year period, so read that row as approximate.9 The spread runs from fewer than 9 days at 100 °F near Temecula to more than 120 in the desert.94

Bachem, a peptide maker, typically ships its peptides at room temperature and says freeze-dried peptides may be kept in a refrigerator at 4 °C for short-term use.13 For longer storage it advises a tightly closed container below -15 °C, and colder still for the long term.13 GenScript, another maker, advises storing freeze-dried peptides at -20 °C away from bright light, and says most stay stable for several years that way, though stability depends on the sequence.14 The same habit works anywhere in the county: bring the parcel in on the day it arrives and store each vial as its product page directs. The storage guide has the detail.

About Riverside

Riverside incorporated on October 11, 1883, in the western part of the county, about 60 miles east of Los Angeles.15 It covers 81.149 square miles of land.6 Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas 92501 and 92503 through 92508 cover nearly all of it, and the small 92521 area lies wholly inside the city. Area 92503 also takes in part of Corona.5 The county took its name from the city when it was formed in 1893, from part of San Bernardino County and a larger part of San Diego County.16

Research and medicine are a large part of the city. The University of California, Riverside has a campus of nearly 1,200 acres, more than 26,000 students and about 1,100 faculty, among them two Nobel Prize winners and 15 members of the National Academies of Science and Medicine.17 Its School of Medicine took its first students in 2013.18 It was created to ease a shortage of health professionals in Inland Southern California and offers PhD and master's degrees in biomedical sciences.18 In 2025, Kaiser Permanente Riverside Medical Center counted 5,817 employees and UC Riverside 5,137.19 Only the County of Riverside (25,345) and Riverside Unified School District (6,562) employed more people in the city.19

The Mission Inn downtown began in 1876 as Frank A. Miller's 12-room adobe guest house.20 It became a California Historical Landmark in 1961 and joined the National Register of Historic Places in 1971.20 California Citrus State Historic Park keeps more than 250 acres of groves and historic buildings in the Arlington Heights area.21 Mount Rubidoux, a 161-acre city park just west of downtown, has 3.5 miles of paved roads closed to cars and hosts the oldest outdoor non-denominational Easter sunrise service in the United States.22

Riverside County had 2,544,916 residents on July 1, 2025, the fourth largest population among California's 58 counties.1 About 17% of its people live outside any incorporated city.1 It spans 7,209 square miles of land.23 The Fourth Supervisorial District alone covers the eastern two-thirds of the county.24 San Jacinto Peak, at 10,834 feet, is the highest peak in the California State Park System.25

Nearby Riverside County pages

By straight-line distance between Census center points, Moreno Valley is about 11 miles east and Corona about 11 miles west-southwest. Temescal Valley is about 13 miles south-southwest, Lakeland Village about 20 miles south and Menifee about 21 miles southeast.6 Farther south are Murrieta, about 28 miles away, and Temecula, about 34 miles away.6

Hemet lies about 11 miles east-northeast of Menifee, and Valle Vista has its own page as well.6 Palm Springs, Palm Desert, La Quinta and Desert Hot Springs are all in the Fourth Supervisorial District, the eastern two-thirds of the county.24 Cities in other counties are on the locations page.

Frequently asked questions

Can semaglutide be delivered to an address in Riverside?

Yes. Semaglutide orders for Riverside addresses ship from the USA and Canada, under the same policy as every order across the United States. The semaglutide page lists the 2 mg, 5 mg vials and their stock status. The shipping page sets out what is and is not yet confirmed about timing and charges, and what to check when a parcel arrives. The vials are sold for laboratory research under the research use policy, and What is Semaglutide? covers the compound itself.

Is there a D2C Peptides location in Riverside County?

No. D2C Peptides has no staffed location in Riverside or anywhere else in the county, so orders arrive by shipping and these pages list no address. Questions about an order go through the contact page. If a parcel arrives damaged, wrong or incomplete, keep it with all of its packaging and follow the steps on the returns page.

How hot does Riverside get for a parcel left outside?

Hot enough to matter in summer. Riverside Municipal Airport averages about 100 days a year at 90 °F or more and about 22 days at 100 °F or more.2 Its August average high is 94.9 °F.3 The desert end of the county is far hotter: the Palm Springs station averages about 123 days a year at 100 °F or more.4 Bring a parcel inside soon after it is delivered.

Which Riverside County places have their own page?

Besides this Riverside hub, there are pages for Corona, Moreno Valley, Temescal Valley, Lakeland Village, Menifee, Murrieta, Temecula, Hemet, Valle Vista, Palm Springs, Palm Desert, La Quinta and Desert Hot Springs. Each one covers delivery, the nearest weather data for storage and the place itself.
